newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-COSTA TO FACE MOYA AFTER ASSURING TOP 10 PLACE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COSTA TO FACE MOYA AFTER ASSURING TOP 10 PLACE.

text.p: Albert Costa earned a semifinal against close friend Carlos Moya in the Barcelona Open by assuring himself a place in the world's top 10 for the first time on Friday.
Costa scored a 6-4 6-2 quarter-final win over Frenchman Cedric Pioline while Moya beat Ukraine's Andrei Medvedev by the same score.
"Both on and off the court it will be tough...facing up to somebody who you spend most time with, here in Barcelona." Moya said.
Costa coped better with difficult conditions against Pioline after a rain stoppage at 5-3 in the first set.
Pioline's resistance crumbled after he squandered two points to break back to 5-5 after the restart.

"It was a complicated moment, but he seemed to fall after that ... and the second set was easier," said Costa, who added that Pioline seemed tired after beating number one seed and holder Thomas Muster the previous day.
Moya nearly let a 5-2 lead slip after a strong start in his match with Medvedev. But the Australian Open finalist cut out the errors in his game and won easily.
Costa could even overhaul Moya in the rankings if he wins the tournament and scores bonus points by beating another Spaniard, world number 19 Alberto Berasategui.
Berasategui, finalist in the 1994 French Open, is clear favourite to prevail in the bottom half of the draw, where he is the only seed left.
He faced a quarter-final later on Friday against Brazil's Fernando Meligeni.
